newsitem.title: USA: KCBT HRW wheat ends higher after stocks decline.
newsitem.headline: KCBT HRW wheat ends higher after stocks decline.

text.p: KCBT May hard red winter wheat futures closed sharply higher in reaction to a sharp drop in deliverable wheat stored in Kansas City, grain traders said.

KCBT reported Tuesday that 1.753 million bushels of deliverable wheat were in Kansas City warehouses as of April 4, down from 2.799 million a week ago. Deliverable stocks in Hutchinson rose to 2.779 million from 1.873 million.
KCBT traders said the increase in Hutchinson stocks was downplayed because much of that wheat will go to exporters or flour mills rather than for delivery.

Additional support was tied to news earlier that Algeria seeks 100,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter or Canadian wheat. But an Algerian official later said it would accept the wheat from suppliers other than just the U.S. or Canada.

Benson Quinn led buying with 3.5 million bushels of May and 1.8 million of July. It sold 1.0 million of July. Prudential Securities bought a total of 3.8 million spread between May and July and sold 4.5 million spread between the two contracts.
KCBT wheat closed up 12-1/4 to five cents, with May up most at $4.24-1/4 a bushel. July closed up seven at $3.95.
Estimated volume was 48.68 million bushels, with 29.515 million in July.
